correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge2\), the cube-edge distance formula gives Walsh blocks on the powered-distance matrix with axial and transverse eigenvalues \(a_s+(n-s-1)b_s\) and \(a_s-b_s\). For \(0<p<1\), Bernstein integral representations show strict negativity of all nonconstant axial modes, while the transverse modes \(-1+J_{n-1}(s+1,p)\) strictly decrease with the Walsh support size \(s\). The unique possible obstruction is the empty-support transverse mode \(S_n(p)-1\), of multiplicity \(n-1\). The function \(S_n\) is strictly increasing from zero to \(2^{n-2}\), which yields the unique cutoff for \(n\ge3\); the four-cycle case \(n=2\) has cutoff one. Above the cutoff this mode is positive. The binomial expectation and bounds \(pB_n\le S_n(p)\le pn^p B_n\) give \(p_n\sim n/2^{n-1}\). The centered Gram rank gives the exact Euclidean embedding dimension. An independent shortest-path/BFS spectral script passes twenty finite comparisons; those are not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The graph metric on edges of the binary \(n\)-cube is a canonical transitive finite metric. Unlike the original Hamming metric on cube vertices, whose negative-type exponent reaches one, its sharp powered-distance exponent decreases as \(p_n\sim n/2^{n-1}\). The theorem supplies an unexpected exponential loss under passage from vertices to edge incidences, proves the responsible Walsh sector and its endpoint \(n-1\)-fold degeneracy, and determines a natural squared-Euclidean embedding dimension. This is an exact, motivated infinite-family boundary, not a fixed-size table entry.
